messages.text: Look at the picture of the top head and tell me what’s wrong with it

Photo shows the pull-down sprayer head removed, with heavy mineral/scale buildup (white/crusty deposits) around the aerator screen and the perimeter where it meets the housing — consistent with hard water scale, possibly mixed with some biofilm/grime given the darker staining near the edge.

For your notes, you could describe it functionally rather than diagnostically: something like "aerator/spray head shows heavy scale and residue buildup around screen and housing" — that documents what's visible without characterizing cause or severity.

A couple things worth grabbing before you move on:
- A shot of the aerator screen itself removed/separated, if it unscrews further — sometimes flow restriction hides behind that layer.
- Quick note on whether water flow/spray pattern was affected when running, since that's observable and useful context alongside the visual.

If you want to flag water quality concerns (hardness, etc.) that's really a homeowner/plumber follow-up question rather than something the photo alone settles.

zoneAttributes.label: Contains mechanical equipment (furnace, panel, water heater, main shutoff…)

items.text: Zone has a canvas (plan scan or wide photos covering all walls)
Ceiling, walls, floor scanned for stains, cracks, slope, separation
Any stain or suspect area metered and the reading recorded
Windows operated, locked, latched; seal-fog noted — pin defects
Representative receptacles tested; every GFCI tripped and reset — pin failures as concerns
Supply/return registers unblocked, airflow confirmed — pin problem registers
Smoke/CO alarms in this zone pinned (manufacture dates photographed)
Anything the owner flagged in this room verified and captured
Window opens fully and stays open without being held
Every sink cabinet opened and inspected **while water runs**; meter if suspect
Fixture shutoffs present, accessible, not weeping
Every drain run and flow observed
Exhaust fan runs, tissue test passed, termination traced to exterior
Caulk and grout condition at all wet joints
Visible framing, beams, posts, sill/rim inspected; movement noted
Foundation walls circuited; every crack pinned, measured, photographed with scale
Insulation type and depth recorded where visible
Visible wiring types noted; knob-and-tube or aluminum flagged as concerns
Concealed areas behind finished surfaces recorded as *not inspected*
Flue/venting traced from appliance to termination
Combustion air provision present and unobstructed
Main water shutoff pinned, photographed wide, tagged
Static water pressure measured (gauge threads onto any hose bib)
Floor drain located, clear, trap primed
Backwater valve located or confirmed absent
Panel make/model recorded; known-issue brands flagged
Sniffer pass at accessible fittings completed
Every appliance in this room has a legible nameplate photo
Anything unidentified pinned as freeform and chat-asked
Wide photo canvas covering the full elevation/area
Grading slope away from foundation; standing water noted
Exterior visible foundation inspected; cracks pinned
Roofline captured by pole cam — slopes, valleys, flashing, edges
Every vent termination pinned and traced to its interior source
Ceiling below every wet room above examined (pre-water-run look)
Basement windows and wells: drainage, security; egress if sleeping zone
Every appliance pinned with its specific type
Range hood vents to exterior (not recirculating) — traced
Pan or floor drain present if above living space
Stair rails both sides, condition, lighting, contrast
House door self-closes and latches; separation intact
CO pathway to living space assessed; alarm coverage
Fuel/chemical storage; extension cords in permanent use
Vermiculite check — if present: STOP, photograph from hatch, disturb nothing, flag suspect ACM
Sheathing condition captured: staining, frost, daylight
Insulation depth measured with ruler in frame
Bath/kitchen/dryer ducts actually exit the attic
Vents open/closed appropriately for season and type
Every downspout pinned at its discharge point
Windows/doors from outside: sills, flashing, seal fog
Chimney pinned: cap, crown, flashing, mortar
Electrical service entry, mast, meter captured
AC/heat pump pinned: level, clearance, line insulation
Where water goes: swales, ditches, culverts
Municipal curb stop pinned if locatable
Septic lids and bed area pinned; surface condition
Bed area: nothing parked, built, or deep-rooted
Retaining walls pinned: lean, drainage, condition
Shoreline/dock captured; erosion comparison positions established
Outbuildings identified; each gets a zone if substantial

sessionItems.text: Emergency shutoff map complete: every Master Spec §1 shutoff and control either pinned or explicitly recorded absent — water main, curb stop, gas, fuel, electrical, water heater, boiler, furnace switch, sump, septic/sewage alarm, solar disconnects, pool disconnect, irrigation, hose bibs, fireplace valve
Alarm coverage judged against the pin set: smoke on every storey and outside sleeping areas; CO adjacent to sleeping areas where fuel-burning appliances, a fireplace, or an attached garage exist
Ceilings below every wet room re-checked **after** all fixtures were run
Every interior exhaust (bath fans, hood, dryer, HRV) matched to a pinned exterior termination
Intake-declared property flags confirmed or corrected on site
Wood-burning appliance pinned and WETT flag recorded
